chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the servant performs i'tikaf, he should fast. And he said: I'tikaf is not valid for less than three days. And stipulate with your Lord during your i'tikaf, just as you stipulate when entering ihram, that He releases you from your i'tikaf in the event of an occurrence, if a cause befalls you from the command of God.

key_terms.إحرام: Ihram: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.استثراء: Stipulation/Condition (implied from اشتراط): A condition set to allow early exit
key_terms.اعتكاف: I'tikaf: Spiritual retreat in a mosque
key_terms.عِلّة: Illness or valid excuse for breaking a ritual obligation

ai.seo_question: What are the minimum duration and conditions for valid i'tikaf in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar establishes the foundational jurisprudence for i'tikaf, mandating fasting and a minimum duration of three days while introducing the 'shart al-ghab' (stipulation of release) to ensure flexibility. By comparing the exit conditions to those of Hajj, it reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with practical ease, ensuring that obligations do not become burdensome due to unforeseen circumstances like illness.
